evidence: Cic. Phil. 2.8: quō mē teste convincēs? (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To call a witness, testem citāre (Cic. Verr. 2.2.146; M-O s.v. subpoena); to come forward as a witness, testis prōdīre (Traupman 197).

terms.grammar: phrase: oculātus, oculāta, oculātum (having eyes) with testis
terms.comment: Plautus’s phrase, set against aurītī, those who have only heard.

terms.gloss: an onlooker: someone present who sees or overhears
terms.comment: The witness who happens to be there, not one called to court: remōtīs arbitrīs, with no one by.

terms.grammar: phrase: testimōnium, testimōniī n. (testimony) with dīcere
evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 102: testimōnium in aliquem dīcere (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Against someone, in aliquem; for someone, prō aliquō (Traupman 197).

phrases.latin: plūris est oculātus testis ūnus quam aurītī decem
phrases.english: one eyewitness is worth more than ten who have only heard

phrases.latin: narrō tibi, haec loca venusta sunt, abdita certē et, sī quid scrībere velīs, ab arbitrīs lībera
phrases.english: I tell you, this place is lovely: hidden, certainly, and free of onlookers, if you want to write
